title: Pixel to Gaussian: Ultra-Fast Continuous Super-Resolution with 2D Gaussian Modeling
claim: Prior methods repeat costly upsampling and decoding for every scale; ours builds one continuous representation and renders each scale cheaply.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; pipelines on left, motivation and plots on right
description: A 2x2 grid. Top-left (a) shows the existing pipeline. An LR photo goes through an encoder, LR features, an upsampler, HR features and a decoder, producing stacked outputs at ×4, ×8 and ×16. Colored per-stage timings (136 ms, 86×N ms, 40×N ms) add up to a total time that grows with N. Bottom-left (c) shows the proposed pipeline. An LR photo goes through a Continuous SR box into a set of colored Gaussian ellipses, then a Rendering box, which outputs the same multi-scale images. Its total time is 229 + 1×N ms. Top-right (b) is a motivation sketch. A continuous real-world surface and a pixelated LR surface are linked by an ISP camera arrow and a ContinuousSR arrow. Bottom-right (d) has a line plot of time against scale number, with a red flat line against a blue rising line, and a grouped bar chart of PSNR gains across four benchmarks. Red text highlights the gains and the speedup.
caption: (a) Leveraging implicit modeling, existing ASSR methods rely on multiple upsampling and decoding steps to reconstruct HR images at different scales, which leads to low efficiency and performance. (b-d) Our method explicitly reconstructs 2D continuous HR signals from LR images in a single pass. Then, fast rendering replaces the time-consuming upsampling and decoding process to reconstruct HR images at different scales, significantly improving both performance (0.90 dB in Manga109) and efficiency (19.5× speedup).
abstract: Arbitrary-scale super-resolution (ASSR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution (HR) images from low-resolution (LR) inputs with arbitrary upsampling factors using a single model, addressing the limitations of traditional SR methods constrained to fixed-scale factors (\textit{e.g.}, $\times$ 2). Recent advances leveraging implicit neural representation (INR) have achieved great progress by modeling coordinate-to-pixel mappings. However, the efficiency of these methods may suffer from repeated upsampling and decoding, while their reconstruction fidelity and quality are constrained by the intrinsic representational limitations of coordinate-based functions. To address these challenges, we propose a novel ContinuousSR framework with a Pixel-to-Gaussian paradigm, which explicitly reconstructs 2D continuous HR signals from LR images using Gaussian Splatting. This approach eliminates the need for time-consuming upsampling and decoding, enabling extremely fast arbitrary-scale super-resolution.
